title: Flattener maxDepth reached mid-document - subtree preserved as verbatim JSON text
rationale: The one structural loss judged defensible, included so the corpus is not a monotone list of defects. maxDepth is a real recursion guard and the truncated subtree is not discarded - flattenObject stores its exact JSON serialisation, so an aware consumer can recover it byte for byte. Classifying this DEFECT would devalue the label everywhere else it appears.
catchesBugClass: That the depth guard fires at the configured boundary and stringifies rather than dropping. Catches an off-by-one at the boundary and any regression where the truncated subtree is replaced by null or a placeholder.
cannotCatch: Nothing marks the resulting String as a truncated subtree, so it is indistinguishable from a user who genuinely stored that JSON text; the only signal is a debug-level log. It also does not cover maxArraySize, which truncates by DISCARDING elements - a very different bargain.

predicted.detail: Re-nesting below the limit is lost; the content is not. The reconstructor leaves the truncated String alone because looksLikeSerializedArray requires a leading bracket.
